groups.identity: Who the row is: ticker, listing and classification.
groups.price_volume: Latest close, traded value, market cap and distance from key price levels.
groups.performance: Percent price changes, and percentile ranks of those changes.
groups.relative_strength: RS ratings within the market, RS line signals, beta and beta-adjusted RS.
groups.trend: Weinstein stage, moving-average alignment and momentum flags.
groups.fundamentals: Earnings and sales growth, with the comparison behind them.
groups.scores: Screener scores and labels. Labels are screening output, not recommendations.
groups.setup_engine: Chart pattern detection, pivot, tightness and breakout readiness.
groups.opportunity: Correction-survivor policy: gates, resilience score and action state.
groups.data_quality: How much data a row had, why fields are null, and scan bookkeeping.

symbol.meaning: Ticker as listed in this market, e.g. NVDA, 7203.T.

company_name.meaning: Company name from the stock universe.

listing_search.meaning: Symbol and company name joined, for text-search rules.
listing_search.note: A filter-rule name the evaluator computes, not a row field. run_screen filters reject it.

market.meaning: Market code, e.g. US, JP, MY.

exchange.meaning: Listing exchange code, e.g. XNYS, XTKS.

currency.meaning: Listing currency; every local_currency field on the row uses it.

ipo_date.meaning: First trading date from fundamentals, else the first stored price bar.
ipo_date.note: A provider floor date or the first stored bar can stand in for it in any market, so do not quote it as a listing date. ipo_score reads the same date for its age points.

ibd_group_rank.meaning: Group's rank by the average RS of its stocks in this market; 1 is strongest.
ibd_group_rank.note: Computed by this project, not published by IBD. Ranks compare within one market only.

ibd_group_rank_date.meaning: Date the group rank was calculated for.

gics_sector.meaning: Sector label from the data provider or the market taxonomy.
gics_sector.note: Not official GICS. Label sets differ by market, e.g. US Financial, JP Financial Services.

gics_industry.meaning: Industry label from the data provider or the market taxonomy.
gics_industry.note: Not official GICS. Label sets differ by market.

market_themes.meaning: Theme tags from the market taxonomy.
market_themes.note: A list, so run_screen filters cannot test its tags.

current_price.meaning: Latest daily close in the listing currency.
current_price.note: This bar can be newer or older than the result's as_of_date. Its date is opportunity_state.as_of_date.

price.meaning: Name screen rules use for current_price.

volume.meaning: Average daily traded value: average daily shares times the latest close.
volume.note: Money, not a share count, in the listing currency. The share average has no single window: Yahoo's averageVolume in the US, a 50-session mean elsewhere, both at the latest fundamentals refresh. It can differ widely from adv_usd, so look at both on a name before quoting liquidity.

listing_aware_volume.meaning: volume, except listing_only rows count as infinite so they pass liquidity minimums.
listing_aware_volume.note: A filter-rule name the evaluator computes, not a row field. run_screen filters reject it.

adv_usd.meaning: Average daily traded value in USD at the latest fundamentals refresh.
adv_usd.note: Prices the shares at market cap divided by shares outstanding, not the latest close, so it can differ widely from volume even for a US stock, and it can be 0. Look at both on a name before quoting liquidity.

market_cap.meaning: Market capitalisation in the listing currency, as of the latest fundamentals refresh.
market_cap.note: Not recomputed from the latest close. Can be 0.

market_cap_usd.meaning: market_cap in USD at the FX rate of the latest fundamentals refresh.

adr_percent.meaning: Mean of (high - low) / close over the last 20 sessions.

gap_percent.meaning: Latest open versus the prior close; positive is a gap up.

volume_surge.meaning: Latest session's shares divided by the prior 50 sessions' average; 1 is normal.

week_52_high_distance.meaning: Percent below the 52-week closing high; 0 is at the high.

week_52_low_distance.meaning: Percent above the 52-week closing low; 0 is at the low.

ema_10_distance.meaning: Percent above (+) or below (-) the 10-day EMA of closes.

ema_20_distance.meaning: Percent above (+) or below (-) the 20-day EMA of closes.

ema_50_distance.meaning: Percent above (+) or below (-) the 50-day EMA of closes.

price_change_1d.meaning: Percent change from the prior close to the latest close.

perf_week.meaning: Percent change in the close over 5 sessions.

perf_month.meaning: Percent change in the close over 21 sessions.

perf_3m.meaning: Percent change in the close over 67 sessions.

perf_6m.meaning: Percent change in the close over 126 sessions.

pct_day.meaning: Percentile rank of price_change_1d among this market's rows; 100 is the biggest gain.
pct_day.note: A rank, not a percent change. Quote price_change_1d for the move.

pct_week.meaning: Percentile rank of perf_week among this market's rows; 100 is the biggest gain.
pct_week.note: A rank, not a percent change. Quote perf_week for the move.

pct_month.meaning: Percentile rank of perf_month among this market's rows; 100 is the biggest gain.
pct_month.note: A rank, not a percent change. Quote perf_month for the move.

price_trend.meaning: 30-session direction: 1 up over 0.5%, -1 down over 0.5%, 0 flat.

price_sparkline_data.meaning: Last 30 closes, scaled so the first is 1.0.
price_sparkline_data.note: In the published JSON only. The MCP tools drop it, so describe_fields reports rows_with_value as null.

rs_rating.meaning: Overall relative strength within this market; 99 is strongest, 1 weakest.
rs_rating.note: Rated rows are in the market's RS universe, set by the StockUniverse.is_common_stock flag, and have an adjusted close at every anchor back 252 sessions. Anything else is null, which is not a weak rating. Some markets' universes include ETFs, so percentiles there are not stock-only. Not comparable across markets.

rs_rating_1m.meaning: Relative strength over 21 sessions within this market; 99 is strongest.
rs_rating_1m.note: Young listings can have this without rs_rating.

rs_rating_3m.meaning: Relative strength over 63 sessions within this market; 99 is strongest.
rs_rating_3m.note: Young listings can have this without rs_rating.

rs_rating_12m.meaning: Relative strength over 252 sessions within this market; 99 is strongest.

rs_as_of_date.meaning: Trading day the RS ratings were calculated for.

beta.meaning: Beta of daily returns against the market's benchmark over up to 252 sessions.
beta.note: Null below 200 sessions, or when the result falls outside the range.

beta_adj_rs.meaning: rs_rating divided by beta, with beta floored at 0.5 and the result capped at 100.
beta_adj_rs.note: Not a 1-99 percentile. Rows can tie at the cap.

beta_adj_rs_1m.meaning: rs_rating_1m divided by beta, with beta floored at 0.5 and the result capped at 100.

beta_adj_rs_3m.meaning: rs_rating_3m divided by beta, with beta floored at 0.5 and the result capped at 100.

beta_adj_rs_12m.meaning: rs_rating_12m divided by beta, with beta floored at 0.5 and the result capped at 100.

rs_line_new_high.meaning: Stock-to-benchmark ratio at a 252-session high on the latest session.
rs_line_new_high.note: False also when benchmark data is missing, not only when the check failed. On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

rs_line_new_high_before_price.meaning: Blue dot on the latest session: RS line at a 252-session high while price is not.
rs_line_new_high_before_price.note: On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

rs_line_blue_dot_recent.meaning: A blue dot fired on any of the last 5 sessions.
rs_line_blue_dot_recent.note: On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

rs_line_new_high_date.meaning: Latest date the RS line made a 252-session high.
rs_line_new_high_date.note: On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

rs_sparkline_data.meaning: Last 30 stock-to-benchmark ratios, scaled so the first is 1.0.
rs_sparkline_data.note: In the published JSON only. The MCP tools drop it, so describe_fields reports rows_with_value as null.

rs_trend.meaning: Slope of the 30-session RS ratio: 1 improving, -1 declining, 0 flat.

stage.meaning: Weinstein stage: 1 basing, 2 advancing, 3 topping, 4 declining.

stage_name.meaning: Name of the stage: Basing, Advancing, Topping or Declining.

ma_alignment.meaning: Close above the 50-day SMA, 50 above 150, 150 above 200, and the 200-day up 1% over a month.

pocket_pivot.meaning: Up day on more volume than any down day of the prior 10 sessions, at or above the 50-day SMA.

power_trend.meaning: Close above the 21-day EMA, EMA above a rising 50-day SMA, and 10 straight closes above the EMA.

eps_growth_qq.meaning: EPS growth for the latest reported period, against the comparison in growth_metric_basis.
eps_growth_qq.note: growth_metric_basis on the row is the only authority for the comparison. quarterly_qoq compares with the prior quarter, comparable_period_yoy with the same period a year earlier. Uncapped, so extreme values occur.

eps_growth_yy.meaning: EPS growth over a year: the latest period against the same period a year earlier.

sales_growth_qq.meaning: Sales growth for the latest reported period, against the comparison in growth_metric_basis.
sales_growth_qq.note: Read growth_metric_basis on the row, as for eps_growth_qq. Uncapped.

sales_growth_yy.meaning: Sales growth over a year: the latest period against the same period a year earlier.

growth_metric_basis.meaning: Comparison behind eps_growth_qq and sales_growth_qq: quarterly_qoq, comparable_period_yoy or unavailable.
growth_metric_basis.note: Set from the gap between the two latest statements. A quarter-sized gap gives quarterly_qoq. Any other gap gives comparable_period_yoy in HK and JP, and unavailable elsewhere. Fewer than two statements give unavailable. A row can hold a growth value with basis unavailable, and its comparison is then unknown.

growth_reporting_cadence.meaning: Cadence inferred from statement dates: quarterly, semiannual, annual, unknown or insufficient_history.

eps_rating.meaning: EPS percentile rank from the fundamentals store; 99 is strongest.
eps_rating.note: Read rows_with_value in describe_fields before relying on it.

peg_ratio.note: The scan does not copy it from fundamentals to the row. Read rows_with_value in describe_fields before relying on it.

composite_score.meaning: Equal-weight average of the screener scores that ran, plus any ipo_bonus.

composite_reason.meaning: Why the composite was adjusted: ipo_uplift, else null.

rating.meaning: Overall label from composite_score and screener passes: Strong Buy, Buy, Watch, Pass, Insufficient Data or Error.
rating.note: A screening label, not a recommendation.

minervini_score.meaning: Minervini template score from RS, stage, MA alignment, 52-week position and VCP; higher is better.

minervini_rating.meaning: Minervini label: Strong Buy, Buy, Watch or Pass.

passes_template.meaning: minervini_score at least 70, rs_rating at least 70 and stage 2.

canslim_score.meaning: CANSLIM score from earnings, new highs, volume, RS and institutional ownership; higher is better.

canslim_rating.meaning: CANSLIM label: Strong Buy, Buy, Watch or Pass.

ipo_score.meaning: IPO score from age, gain since listing, stability, volume and revenue growth.
ipo_score.note: Computed for seasoned stocks too, so a value does not mean a recent IPO. Its age points read ipo_date, which can be a provider floor date or the first stored bar, so a seasoned name can score high.

ipo_bonus.meaning: Points added to composite_score for a strong ipo_score with under 252 bars of history.

custom_score.meaning: Percent of points earned on the default custom filters: price, RS, liquidity, market cap, growth, MA alignment.
custom_score.note: Its price band is in local currency, so scores are not comparable across markets.

volume_breakthrough_score.meaning: Record-volume score: a 5-year, 1-year or since-IPO volume high in the last 5 sessions, decayed by age.

volume_breakthrough_rating.meaning: Label from how many record-volume checks hit: Strong Buy, Buy, Watch or Pass.

vcp_detected.meaning: vcp_score at least 65, with contracting pullbacks and price tight near recent highs.

vcp_score.meaning: Score from pullback depth, volume, tightness and ATR contraction; 0 with too few bases.

vcp_num_bases.meaning: Consolidation bases the VCP detector found.

vcp_pivot.meaning: Highest closing-price peak of the last two bases, in the listing currency.
vcp_pivot.note: The detector sees only closes, so this is not an intraday high.

vcp_ready_for_breakout.note: Also true when price is already far above the pivot.

vcp_contraction_ratio.meaning: Share of successive pullbacks shallower than the one before; 1 means all of them.
vcp_contraction_ratio.note: 0 can mean it was never calculated, because a row with fewer than three bases gets 0. Check vcp_num_bases.

vcp_atr_score.meaning: Contraction score from a close-to-close volatility proxy: the 14-session mean absolute change in the close, recent against about 30 sessions ago; higher is tighter.
vcp_atr_score.note: Not true range, because the detector sees only closes.

se_setup_score.note: It does not read the stock's stage, so declining stocks can score high. A score alone is not a setup.

se_quality_score.meaning: Quality of the primary detected pattern; higher is better.

se_readiness_score.meaning: Breakout readiness of the primary detected pattern; higher is better.

se_setup_ready.meaning: True only when no check failed, across every detector and every setup gate: scores, early zone, ATR, volume dry-up, RS and trend context.
se_setup_ready.note: A detector that found nothing counts as a failed check, so a false does not say a stock failed a setup gate. true_rows in describe_fields counts the true rows in this publish and does not say why a row is false.

se_pattern_primary.meaning: Best detected pattern, e.g. cup_with_handle, three_weeks_tight, high_tight_flag, nr7_inside_day.
se_pattern_primary.note: The best candidate is named even below the confidence floor, so a name alone is not a setup. A preset match means only that its rules passed, so check stage, se_in_early_zone, se_pivot_date and action_state before calling it a setup.

se_pattern_confidence.meaning: Detector confidence in the primary pattern; 100 is highest.
se_pattern_confidence.note: It does not read the stock's stage, so declining stocks can score high. A score alone is not a setup.

se_pivot_price.meaning: Breakout level of the primary pattern, in the listing currency.
se_pivot_price.note: The pivot can be years old, so check se_pivot_date.

se_pivot_type.meaning: What the pivot level is, e.g. handle_high, flag_high, tight_area_high.

se_distance_to_pivot_pct.meaning: Close against the pivot: positive above it, negative below it.
se_distance_to_pivot_pct.note: The pivot can be years old, so check se_pivot_date.

se_in_early_zone.meaning: Close from 2% below to 3% above the pivot.
se_in_early_zone.note: The pivot can be years old, so check se_pivot_date.

se_extended_from_pivot.meaning: Close more than 10% above the pivot.

se_base_length_weeks.meaning: Length of the primary pattern's base.

se_base_depth_pct.meaning: Depth or width of the base; what it measures depends on the pattern.
se_base_depth_pct.note: Cup depth, flag depth, tight-range width or distance from high. Can exceed 100 on three_weeks_tight rows, so it is not always a drawdown.

se_support_tests_count.note: Only rows whose primary pattern is first_pullback have it.

se_atr14_pct.meaning: 14-session Wilder ATR as a percent of the close.

se_bb_width_pctile_252.meaning: Percentile of Bollinger width within the stock's own last 252 sessions; low is tight.

se_volume_vs_50d.meaning: Latest shares divided by a 50-session average that includes the latest session.

se_up_down_volume_ratio_10d.meaning: Up-day volume over down-day volume across 10 sessions; above 1 means more up volume.
se_up_down_volume_ratio_10d.note: The denominator floors at 1e-9, so 10 sessions without a down day give huge values. Use medians.

se_quiet_days_10d.meaning: Sessions of the last 10 with volume under 80% of its 50-session average and range under ATR.

se_rs_line_new_high.meaning: RS line at a 252-session high on the latest session, as the setup engine sees it.
se_rs_line_new_high.note: On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

se_rs_line_blue_dot.meaning: RS line at a 252-session high on the latest session while price is not.
se_rs_line_blue_dot.note: On a short history the window is whatever bars exist, so check history_bars.

se_timeframe.meaning: Payload label that defaults to daily, whatever bars the pattern used.
se_timeframe.note: It does not give the pattern's timeframe. three_weeks_tight and cup_with_handle use weekly bars.

correction_survivor.meaning: Passes the leadership, trend, structure, liquidity and freshness gates, with all required evidence.
correction_survivor.note: False when a gate failed and also when evidence is missing. failed_checks in opportunity_state names which for a row. true_rows in describe_fields counts the true rows in this publish and does not say why a row is false.

resilience_score.meaning: Sum of the five 0-20 pillars in opportunity_state's score_pillars.
resilience_score.note: Null unless every input is known, and se_tight_closes_count exists only on three_weeks_tight rows, so rows with any other primary pattern are null.

action_state.meaning: Policy state, first match wins: exit_risk, event_risk, extended, data_limited, then setup_ready or watch.
action_state.note: A policy label, not advice. exit_risk means a hard flag: the close is below the 50-day SMA. data_limited is usually a data gap, not a verdict on the stock. setup_ready needs correction_survivor, se_setup_ready and se_in_early_zone together, so its absence from describe_fields values says nothing about the stocks.

opportunity_state.meaning: Evidence behind action_state: gates passed and failed, score pillars, metrics and data availability.
opportunity_state.note: Its as_of_date is the row's last price bar, which can differ from the scan's as_of_date.

is_scannable.meaning: False when no screener could score the row: too little history, or no RS rating.

history_bars.meaning: Daily price bars available to the scan.

field_availability.meaning: Why fields are null: status and reason_code per field, for ownership, short interest and growth.
field_availability.note: In the published JSON only. The MCP tools drop it, so describe_fields reports rows_with_value as null.

data_status.meaning: Scan outcome: complete, insufficient_history or error.

scan_mode.meaning: History tier: full at 252+ bars, ipo_weighted at 30-251, listing_only below 30.

applicable_screeners.meaning: Screeners this row had enough data for.

unavailable_screeners.meaning: Screeners this row did not have enough data for.

matched_groups.meaning: Setup groups matched by a query's filter expression.

rs_formula_version.meaning: Version of the RS formula behind the ratings.

market_rs_run_id.meaning: Internal id of the market RS run.

rs_universe_size.meaning: Stocks in the market's RS ranking, which can be fewer than its rows.
